ORAL JUDGMENT : (Per : Z. A. Haq, J.)
 1] Heard.
 2] Food Inspector, Food and Drugs Administration (M.S.),
Akola, filed a complaint against the applicants and Biharilal Basweshwarlal Hada under Section 7(i)
read with Section 2(ia)(a) punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(ii), and Section 7(i) read with Section 2(ia)(m) punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of the Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short "the Act of 1954") contending that the accused (applicants and Biharilal) committed offence while manufacturing for sale, distributing for sale, stocking for sale and selling adulterated food articles i.e. Chana Dal.

entities.text:
Food Inspector, Food and Drugs Administration (M.S.),
Akola
entities.label: RESPONDENT

entities.text: Prevention of the Food Adulteration Act, 1954
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3] According to the complainant, Shri B. V. Kulkarni, Food Inspector had visited the premises of accused No.1 - Biharilal on 29 th August, 1994 and had drawn sample of Chana Dal and had sent it for analysis to the Public Analyst, Public Health Laboratory, Amravati.

According to the complainant, report of Public Analyst dated 10 th October, 1994 was received by the Food Inspector on 17 th October 1994, and as the report stated that Chana Dal was not of the standard as required by the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 Judgment 3 Cr.Appln3106.2009.odt complaint came to be filed against the three accused, the accused No.1 - Biharilal being the seller and accused Nos.2 and 3 being the manufacturer.
The complaint was filed on 07th August, 1997.

4] The applicants (accused Nos.2 and 3) have approached this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure praying that the Reg.Cri.Case No.769/1997 registered against them before the learned Judicial Magistrate, First Class be quashed.

Various grounds are raised by the applicants (accused Nos.2 and 3), one on it being that because of the delay in lodging the complaint, valuable right of the applicants conferred by Section 13(2) of the Act of 1954 is taken away.

5 ] On examining the submission made on behalf of the applicants (accused Nos.2 and 3) relying on the provisions of Section 13(2) of the Act of 1954, though we find that such submission would not have assisted the applicants in 1997 when the complaint came to be filed, as shelflife was not prescribed for the food article i.e. Chana Dal, however, now after 25 years of seizure of the food article, because of delay in service of summons on the applicants (accused Nos.2 and 3)
and then because of pendency of this criminal application and the interim order granted by this Court, it is clear that the right conferred Judgment 4 Cr.Appln3106.2009.odt on the accused by Section 13(2) of the Act of 1954, is taken away.
Hence, on this point itself the complaint filed against the applicants (accused Nos.2 and 3) has to be quashed.

sentences.text:
Hence, the following order is passed :
 (i) The proceedings of Reg.Cri.Case No.769/1997 pending before learned 10 th Joint Civil Judge, Junior Division and Judicial Magistrate, First Class,
Akola against the applicants (accused Nos.2 and 3) are quashed.

entities.text: 10 th Joint Civil Judge, Junior Division
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: (ii) The Reg.Cri.Case No.769/1997 pending against accused Biharilal Basweshwarlal Hada shall proceed further, according to law.
Rule is made absolute accordingly.
No costs.

It is noticed in almost all the matters filed under the Seeds Act 1966, The Insecticide Act 1968, The Drugs and Cosmetic Act, 1940 and the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (now The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006) that there is provision like Section Judgment 5 Cr.Appln3106.2009.odt 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 conferring right on the accused to get the sample of the seized articles analyzed through Central or Public Laboratory.

The officers who file the complaint before learned Magistrate, deliberately delay the filing of the complaint, and the complaint is filed just a couple of weeks before the expiry of shelflife of the seized articles and then the summons is served on the accused after the expiry of the shelflife of the seized articles and then the accused approaches this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure complaining that its valuable statutory right of getting the sample of seized article analyzed through Central or Public Laboratory is frustrated and this Court has no option but to quash the proceedings.
It is noticed that this is the modus operandi of the accused and the officer filing the complaint and also the police officers entrusted with the job of serving summons/warrants on the accused.
There are no guidelines providing for time limit for filing of such complaints and providing for penal action against the erring officers who are authorized to file complaint.

The Government of Maharashtra and the Union of India are directed to issue guidelines regulating the procedure for filing of the criminal complaint against the accused under the provisions of Judgment 6 Cr.Appln3106.2009.odt enactments similar/analogous to Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
The affidavit of compliance shall be filed on record of this criminal petition till 30th June, 2020.
Authenticated copy of this order be given to learned Government Pleader, Nagpur Bench of Bombay High Court and learned Assistant Solicitor General of India, Nagpur.

(M. G. GIRATKAR, J.) (Z. A. HAQ, J.)
